title: A module-valued functor with flat base change splits into weight spaces over a graded algebra
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file adequate.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a module-valued functor F on Alg_A such that F(B) tensor_B B' = F(B') for every flat B -> B', the lemma shows that for a graded A-algebra B the module F(B) is the direct sum of its weight spaces, and that the image of F(B_0) -> F(B) lies in the weight zero part (statement lines 532-544). The proof is a displayed coefficient comparison: given x in F(B), the free extension B -> B[t, t^-1] splits F(B[t, t^-1]) as a direct sum of copies of F(B), and the section t -> 1 recovers x as the sum of its coefficients; then the commutative square of graded algebra maps a, a', f, g in the variables t and s is used to identify F(a)(x_k) = t^k x_k, which is exactly the weight statement; finally the last claim follows by comparing the two composite maps B_0 -> B -> B[t, t^-1] (proof lines 546-592). The level is H3: a genuine computation with a deliberately chosen two-variable diagram, every step displayed.
